Leveraging ultra-sensitive mass spectrometry-based phosphoproteomics, my first objective is to develop and benchmark a first-of-its-kind framework for measuring the response of peripheral blood mononuclear cells to drug perturbations (PerturbPhos). We will apply PerturbPhos to a cohort of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients to demonstrate that drug-induced perturbations are personal and reflect the individual’s disease background. Moreover, I hypothesize that ex vivo perturbations functionalize a patient’s phosphoproteome, which will allow us to investigate patient-specific mechanisms of drug action and associate many previously uncharacterized phosphorylation sites in the human proteome with drug response. We will perform a CRISPR-mediated based editor screen to functionally validate the latter at scale. The third objective is to demonstrate, on the example of AML patients, that computational integration of PerturbPhos profiles with clinical data, public databases and literature can rationalize treatment recommendations. Collectively, these results will shed mechanistic light on drug response heterogeneity, underscore the potential of proteomics to provide actionable insights for treating individual cancer patients and advocate for adopting a multi-omics perspective in precision medicine.

title: Data driven Excellence in Training of Epidemiological, Clinical, Technological and Innovative Virus Experts
objective: Emerging and re-emerging viral infections place a major and growing burden on health systems, economies and societies in Europe. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed how fragmented diagnostics, surveillance and data analysis, combined with shortages of cross-disciplinary experts, limit Europe’s ability to anticipate and manage new threats. Despite rapid advances in genomics, bioinformatics and digital surveillance, most responses remain reactive, focused on known pathogens and siloed data streams, rather than on integrated, predictive epidemic intelligence.  DETECTIVE aims to close this gap by training 14 Doctoral Candidates (DCs) to develop and apply next-generation tools for early detection of emerging viruses, assessment of host and population risk, and translation of complex data into real-time, evidence-based action. The network will combine advanced virology, organoid and culture models, next-generation sequencing, wastewater and blood-donor surveillance, and multi-omics with AI driven analytics, bioinformatics and epidemic modelling. Unlike conventional programmes focused on single disciplines or pathogens, DETECTIVE targets the full pathway from pathogen detection and mechanistic understanding to integrated surveillance and clinical and public health decision support. Through this integrated field of data driven epidemic intelligence, DETECTIVE will promote a shift from reactive outbreak control to proactive risk assessment, early warning and targeted intervention. DCs will be trained in an intersectoral environment spanning universities, hospitals, public health institutes, regulators and industry, acquiring both cutting edge scientific skills and key transferable competences. The programme will strengthen European preparedness and resilience by delivering new tools, standards and decision frameworks for epidemic surveillance and response, while creating a new generation of virus experts able to bridge laboratory science, data analytics and public health practic

title: INNOVATIVE RATIONAL PROMOTER BREEDING FOR CLIMATE RESILIENT CROPS INPROBED
objective: INPROBED pioneers a paradigm shift in plant biotechnology by moving from conventional gene editing to precision promoter engineering, by adapting natural gene regulation to build stress resilience and nutritional quality into food crops. The project will develop the first predictive “promoter design platform” for tomato, integrating single-cell MOA-seq with deep-learning models to map and reprogram cis-regulatory elements that control plant responses to heat, drought, and micronutrient limitation. This approach enables precise, predictable, and regulation-compatible genome edits that enhance resilience without compromising growth or yield.Using CRISPR-based promoter editing, INPROBED will generate tomato lines that accumulate more zinc, iron, and provitamin D₃ while maintaining stable performance under stress. These lines will be validated through multi-omics analysis and high-throughput phenotyping, resulting in pre-breeding of proof-of-concept lines for semi-field trials.The consortium unites world-leading expertise in genomics, cistromics, and translational crop science: Heinrich Heine University advances promoter discovery and single-cell analysis; Wageningen University and the Weizmann Institute lead nutritional and metabolic engineering; KeyGene leads the genome editing, single cell technology development and ensures rapid integration into breeding pipelines; and PLANeT Biotech drives phenotyping, validation, and commercialization.INPROBED is a generic technology platform enabling crop improvement via rational promoter engineering in a crop-agnostic manner.

title: Translating Extracellular Vesicle Communication into AI Guided Breeding and Smart Biofertilization
objective: Climate change increasingly exposes crops to drought and indirectly aggravates nutrient limitations by disrupting soil moisture and nutrient cycling. These combined stresses can cut cereal yields by up to 50% in Europe, while low fertilizer efficiency accelerates soil degradation, biodiversity loss, and nitrogen-driven green-house gas emissions, further amplifying climate change. EVOLVE pioneers a breakthrough biotechnology that translates extracellular vesicle (EV)–mediated rhizosphere signaling into actionable breeding and bio-input tools to enhance wheat resilience, nutrient efficiency, and grain quality under combined drought × nitrogen deficiency.Built on the hypothesis that EV-associated small RNAs and metabolites released by roots steer soil microbiomes, EVOLVE decodes and applies EV communication to shape beneficial plant–microbe interactions. Using wheat as the target crop and barley as a diploid reference, the project will:(1) identify EV cargos coordinating root–microbiome interactions and nutrient cycling under single and combined stresses;(2) apply AI-driven multi-omics integration to link EV cargos with plant performance and microbial functions;(3) translate molecular markers into double haploid breeding pipelines for rapid fixation and combination of complementary stress resistances; and(4) develop synthetic and algal-derived EVs via microfluidic encapsulation as programmable, bio-based fertilizers.Validated in aeroponic and soil systems reproducing drought, nitrogen limitation, and their combination, EVOLVE will deliver a TRL4 proof-of-concept for non-transgenic EV-guided breeding tools and next-generation biofertilizers that enhance NUE and WUE by ≥10–15%, stabilize yields, improve grain quality, and reduce N2O emissions and nitrate leaching. By merging EV biology, predictive breeding, and synthetic delivery, EVOLVE defines a new route toward climate-resilient, high-quality, low-emission cereal production in Europe.

title: Doctoral Training in Ruminant Microbiome Science:Developing Evidence-Based Interventions for Sustainable Food Production and Climate Change Mitigation
objective: RUMEN-INNOVATE will establish a pioneering Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network that advances sustainable ruminant agriculture through microbiome-based innovations. Building on extensive existing datasets, this network will train the next generation of scientists to revolutionise direct-fed microbial applications and sustainable ruminant production.The programme operates through three integrated pillars: Discovery & Prediction using machine learning and multi-omics to identify key microbiome-host interactions; Validation & Mechanistic Understanding through controlled studies and synthetic microbial community design; and Translation & Implementation developing real-world diagnostic tools, delivery systems, and on-farm technologies.RUMEN-INNOVATE will train doctoral candidates across European institutions with industry partnerships spanning nutrition companies, dairy, and meat sectors. Researchers will gain expertise in computational biology, experimental validation, and commercial application—creating versatile scientists capable of bridging laboratory discovery with agricultural implementation.The network addresses critical global challenges: feeding a growing population sustainably, reducing greenhouse gas emissions from livestock, and developing alternatives to antibiotics in animal agriculture. By advancing microbiome-based solutions, RUMEN-INNOVATE will deliver innovations that enhance animal health, improve production efficiency, and support environmental sustainability.Through international, interdisciplinary, and intersectoral collaboration, the network will produce breakthrough technologies, highly skilled researchers, and direct pathways for microbiomics innovations to reach farmers and consumers, positioning Europe as the global leader in ruminant microbiome science.

title: Advancing syphilis control: elucidating novel dynamics for vaccine target discovery
objective: Treponema pallidum (TP), the causative agent of syphilis, along with other pathogenic spirochetes, forms a distinct evolutionary clade with unique features including periplasmic endo-flagella, minimal genomes, and outer membranes lacking lipopolysaccharides. These features enable TP to navigate viscous environments, breach biological barriers, and evade host immune responses, leading to severe diseases affecting over 7 million people globally each year. While vaccine development is vital to controlling syphilis, there is currently little consensus on effective vaccine targets. Clinically relevant strains and infection models are needed to deepen our understanding of TP's biology, without which vaccine progress will be challenging. This is urgent since syphilis infects 1 million pregnant women and causes 200,000 stillbirths annually, making it the second leading cause of stillbirths after malaria.Research on TP is hindered by its dependence on host cells for growth, complicating in vitro cultivation and leaving critical questions unanswered. ASCEND will address these gaps by unraveling TP's distinctive biology and host interactions, using multi-omics approaches and cutting-edge techniques like spatial transcriptomics. Specifically, I will identify TP's host dependencies and optimize axenic (cell-free) culture conditions to isolate and grow TP directly from clinical samples, enabling the use of clinically relevant strains for experimentation. Furthermore, I will identify TP adhesins and characterize their roles in attachment and cell cycle, positioning them as prime vaccine candidates to block infection at its earliest stage. Finally, skin organoids will be employed, for the first time, to investigate host-pathogen interactions in 3D under conditions that better mimic human disease than monolayer culture. Ultimately, ASCEND will seek to identify effective vaccine candidates and improve understanding of TP biology to combat syphilis

title: Training a New Generation to Decode the Human Cis-Regulatory Genome
objective: Decoding how the “non-coding” genome controls gene expression is one of the grand challenges of modern biomedicine. Most disease-associated variants fall in regulatory DNA, yet their effects on gene regulation remain largely unpredictable, limiting diagnosis, risk stratification and the design of safe gene and cell therapies. cisCODE is an MSCA Doctoral Network that will train 15 Doctoral Candidates to crack the cis-regulatory code by combining cutting-edge genomics with artificial intelligence and synthetic biology.The network gathers 13 academic partners, completed with 9 non-academic partners across experimental and computational disciplines. Together, they will (i) decode the sequence “grammar” and modular function of cis-regulatory elements, (ii) map the rules of communication and compatibility between distal enhancers and promoters in three-dimensional chromatin, and (iii) build causal, predictive enhancer-based gene regulatory networks in health, stress, inflammation and cancer. Doctoral projects will leverage single-cell multi-omics, high-throughput functional assays, advanced 3D genome profiling and next-generation AI models to move from descriptive catalogues to mechanistic and predictive understanding.cisCODE is also a training engine for Europe. A structured, international and intersectoral programme will provide Doctoral Candidates with personalised research and career development plans, network-wide schools, secondments in industry and clinics, and dedicated training in open science, data stewardship, ethics and innovation.By delivering new models, datasets and synthetic regulatory tools openly to the community, cisCODE will accelerate interpretation of regulatory variants, support the rational design of precision therapies, and consolidate Europe’s leadership at the interface of regulatory genomics, artificial intelligence and personalised medicine.

title: OmegaTree: MAS-10® Enabled Metabolomics and AI-Driven Precision Nutrition and Health Analytics Platform
objective: OmegaTree is developing MAS-10®, a patented volumetric microsampling system enabling accurate, hematocrit-independent blood collection from a simple finger-prick, stable at room temperature and validated in licensed laboratories. Unlike dried blood spot or VAMS devices, MAS-10® is compatible with advanced metabolomics (LC-MS/MS, GC-MS, ICP-MS) and is being expanded to measure amino acids, fatty acids, SCFAs, organic acids, trace elements, and oxidative stress markers (8-OHdG). An AI-driven reporting platform integrates these biomarkers with nutrition data to deliver personalized dietary and health insights. Early pilots confirm compatibility with next-generation sequencing, opening the path toward multi-omics precision health. The project addresses the urgent global need for scalable solutions against obesity, diabetes, and other non-communicable diseases, directly aligned with UN SDG 3 and the EU Precision Nutrition Pathfinder Challenge. Target users include individuals, clinics, dietitians, functional medicine experts, wellness units in hospitals, supplement companies, and corporate health programs. With CE-IVD self-declared kits, UTS registration, national funding, and ethics-approved clinical trials, MAS-10® is ready for TRL 6 validation. The core team combines expertise in biostatistics, medical biochemistry, engineering, nutrition & dietetics, analytical chemistry, and molecular biology. It is supported by Erciyes Technopark and Technology Transfer Office for IP management, business development, and commercialization, alongside external regulatory consultants. Over the next 12–24 months, we will optimize the device, expand biomarker panels, conduct a randomized controlled trial in obese individuals, enhance AI reporting, and refine business/regulatory pathways. This Pre-Accelerator project will deliver a clinically validated, market-ready precision nutrition platform at TRL 6, while laying the foundation for TRL 7–9 scale-up and an EIC Accelerator application.

title: HARPNET – Harnessing Resolution Pharmacology for Next-Generation Therapeutics
objective: Chronic inflammatory diseases and their comorbidities pose a major global health burden, with conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD) affecting hundreds of millions worldwide. Current anti-inflammatory therapies alleviate symptoms but rarely restore tissue homeostasis, leaving patients at risk of persistent inflammation and long-term damage. Addressing this challenge requires researchers trained not only in classical immunology and pharmacology but also in the emerging field of Resolution Pharmacology, which aims to activate endogenous pathways that terminate inflammation and promote tissue repair. Yet the interdisciplinary expertise required, spanning resolution biology, GPCR signalling, advanced multi-omics, systems analysis, and translational development, is not available within existing programmes, creating a critical skills gap that limits progress.HARPNET addresses this unmet need through an innovation-driven training programme uniting 14 beneficiaries and 11 associated partners. Fifteen Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will be embedded in cross-disciplinary teams that co-develop cutting-edge methodologies, including integrated multi-omic pipelines, systems-level disease models, and next-generation approaches to target pro-resolving pathways. This will equip DCs with the scientific, technical, and translational competencies required to drive mechanism-based therapeutic innovation.Using RA and RA-associated CVD as clinically relevant models, HARPNET will deliver hands-on, systems-level, cross-sectoral training across academic, clinical, and industrial settings. Through this comprehensive and co-creative programme, DCs will bridge discovery research with therapeutic development, generating transferable tools and knowledge that extend beyond the network. HARPNET will strengthen Europe’s long-term capacity to lead in Resolution Pharmacology and to train the next generation of innovators in inflammation research.

title: A metabolic-based defense strategy against malaria
objective: Human diseases can emerge from evolutionary trade-offs, when the fitness advantage associated with natural selection of a trait is balanced out by another trait that reduces fitness. KILLBILL builds on this biological principle by reframing jaundice as an adaptive defense mechanism. Regarded historically as a symptom, we discovered that unconjugated bilirubin, the hallmark of jaundice, provides dual protection against malaria: it kills Plasmodium while shielding host tissues from ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death pathway causing organ damage. These salutary effects extend beyond malaria, towards sickle cell disease - an inherited hemolytic condition shaped by malaria. We hypothesize that bilirubin contributes to sickle hemoglobin's anti-malarial effect while protecting from hemolysis-induced pathology in sickle cell disease. KILLBILL will define the molecular logic of this dual protection with the potential to translate it into an evolution-informed therapeutic framework. This will be achieved through innovative experimental systems, encompassing genetically modified mice with controlled levels of jaundice and transgenic parasites reporting on bilirubin sensing to link bilirubin targeting with parasite outcomes. Multi-omics and computational modeling will map parasite and host bilirubin-responsive pathways, while proteome-wide assays and genetic manipulation will validate these functionally. We will zoom in the host, focusing on pathways whereby bilirubin regulates ferroptosis and anti-malaria immunity, probing how bilirubin contributes to the anti-malarial effect of sickle hemoglobin and validating ferroptosis as a therapeutic target in both malaria and sickle cell disease. KILLBILL explores bilirubin-responsive molecular vulnerabilities to deliver the blueprints for future dual-action therapeutic strategies reducing pathogen burden and protecting host tissues, towards evolution-informed drug discovery in malaria and beyond.

title: Plant root coordinated signalling during microbiota establishment
objective: Multicellular organisms host diverse microbes that play vital roles in their health and crop resilience. The host and its microbes form intricate ecosystems characterized by heterogeneity and multidimensionality, hindering the mechanistic understanding needed for targeted management. The ambitious challenge is to disentangle the complexity of signalling events involved in plant root-microbiota assembly to achieve an optimal cost-benefit outcome from these cross-kingdom alliances. The central hypothesis is that a crosstalk between different microbe-induced signalling pathways is established and governs the formation of environmental micro-niches on or inside the root where specific microbial infections occur. ProMIC will identify plant genes and pathways that coordinate the formation of these niches in space and time. We will pioneer innovative approaches based on synthetic gene circuits, activation of targeted pathways, and tailored microbial infections. These will be combined with state-of-the-art bacterial genetics, spatial omics, and advanced cell biology to study the intricate signalling networks driving microbiota assembly at an unprecedented level of granularity. Lotus japonicus is our testbed, as it engages in multiple symbioses and associations with diverse soil microbes. ProMIC capitalizes on the substantial resources for genetic and molecular studies of host-associated microbiota in Lotus to establish a framework for understanding how multicellular organisms host complex microbial communities, a stepping stone for the efficient use of microbial solutions in sustainable crop production. ProMIC builds on my well-established expertise in plant-microbe interactions of varying complexity and on our fundamental discoveries from receptor signalling studies to provide molecular knowledge that complements the current systems-level exploration of the field.

title: Immune cell states as building blocks  of the plant immune system
objective: ImmuneCellStates is a high-risk/high-gain project to redefine the framework of plant immunity, positioning immune cell states as its fundamental building blocks. Unlike mammals, plants lack specialized immune cells. Instead, individual cells, normally dedicated to non-immune functions, transition their states through diverse mechanisms to engage in defense during pathogen attack. My recent work combining single-cell multiomics and spatial transcriptomics revealed that plants flexibly deploy molecularly distinct immune cell states across infected tissues. Yet their diversity, regulation, and function remain poorly understood.Recent technological breakthroughs offer a path to close this gap. I developed a method to map gene expression in 3D plant tissues at unprecedented resolution. In parallel, deep learning now reveals the regulatory logic of cell-specific gene expression, and genome editing enables multiplexed perturbations to dissect complex traits masked by genetic redundancy. However, these methods have yet to be deployed to their full potential.ImmuneCellStates will unite these transformative technologies in an innovative framework to chart, decode, and functionally test immune cell states in plants, an approach not yet attempted. The project tackles three linked but independent aims:(1) CELL STATES: Map immune cell states with 3D spatial context and pathogen proximity.(2) REGULATION: Decode cis-regulatory logic driving cell state-specific immune gene expression.(3) FUNCTION: Perturb cell state regulators to test causal roles in resistance.This interdisciplinary approach will bridge molecular and cellular views of plant immunity, laying the groundwork for a mechanistic understanding of a multicellular system of programmable immune cell states. ImmuneCellStates will transform our view of plant immunity and provide a widely applicable framework to study cell states, opening new paths for discovery in plant biology and crop engineering.

title: Development of an untargeted spatial omics approach with molecular spatial resolution
objective: The next frontier in the life sciences is to map not only the composition but also the spatial organization of entire transcriptomes, genomes, and proteomes at molecular resolution. Existing approaches either achieve high resolution without scalability, scalability without resolution, or breadth without unbiased detection. Targeted methods such as MERFISH, seqFISH+, or FLASH-PAINT rely on affinity reagents and remain blind to unknown molecules, while untargeted approaches such as Light-Seq or DBiT-Seq require complex hardware, are diffraction-limited, and are restricted to nucleic acids.The Molecular Atlas Project (MAP) will overcome these barriers by developing the first untargeted, scalable, and super-resolved spatial omics strategy. MAP introduces randomized DNA barcodes that are assembled directly on molecules in situ and read out by sequential imaging with FLASH-PAINT. This strategy enables unique labeling of every RNA or DNA molecule in a sample, with subsequent identification by sequencing and correlation with spatial imaging data. In parallel, FLASH-RESI will achieve Ångström-level resolution in a single imaging round, enabling barcoded imaging even in dense molecular environments. Finally, MAP will pioneer the extension of this strategy to proteins by attaching DNA barcodes to protein functional groups and reading them out by nanopore-based protein fingerprinting. This objective will establish, for the first time, a route to unbiased spatial proteomics with molecular precision.By combining accessibility (compatible with standard microscopes and sequencing platforms) with disruptive conceptual advances, MAP will transform spatial biology from targeted imaging into truly comprehensive, untargeted spatial omics, catalyzing discovery across cancer biology, neuroscience, microbiology, immunology, and medicine.

title: Astrocytic exhaustion underlies chronic progression in autoimmune inflammation of the central nervous system
objective: Progressive disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains an unmet clinical challenge, largely resistant to current immunomodulatory therapies targeting acute inflammation. AXhaustMS addresses a fundamental gap by investigating astrocytic exhaustion as a novel cellular mechanism underlying chronic progression in autoimmune central nervous system (CNS) inflammation. I hypothesize that astrocytes, key regulators of CNS homeostasis, enter a dysfunctional “exhaustion” state driven by chronic bystander activation, disrupting essential metabolic support networks with neurons, oligodendrocytes, and microglia. Using the spontaneous opticospinal encephalomyelitis (OSE) mouse model that recapitulates key pathological features of progressive MS, I will comprehensively define the molecular and epigenomic signatures of exhausted astrocytes and their disrupted cellular communication networks across distinct CNS compartments and disease stages (Aim 1). I will then dissect how activation context – bystander versus direct targeting – determines astrocyte fate towards either durable, sensitized states or maladaptive exhaustion leveraging exclusive T cell receptor (TCR) transgenic mouse systems and controlled T cell transfer models (Aim 2). Finally, I will validate the functional impact of exhaustion markers through ex vivo and in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-mediated gene perturbation strategies, testing therapeutic reversibility (Aim 3).This meticulous approach integrates innovative animal models, state-of-the-art multi-omics, and advanced gene editing to elucidate astrocytic dysfunction as a key driver of progressive MS. AXhaustMS has transformative potential to shift the treatment paradigm from immune suppression to cellular rehabilitation, offering new avenues for therapeutic intervention in MS and related neurodegenerative diseases characterized by chronic glial dysfunction.

title: XENObiotic-based PREDiction platform of inter-individual differences in drug metabolism
objective: Inter-individual variability in drug metabolism remains a major barrier to clinical practice and drug development, often leading to adverse reactions, therapeutic inefficacy, and costly trial failures. While genetics explain only part of this variability, the contribution of the gut microbiome remains largely underestimated. The ERC-StG PREDICT-CARE project has shown that dietary (poly)phenols, a large family of plant xenobiotics metabolised through pathways that partly overlap with those involved in the metabolism of several drugs, give rise to reproducible metabolic phenotypes, defined by consistent inter-individual differences in the production of circulating phenolic metabolites and shaped by host genetics and gut microbial activity. These metabolic profiles may therefore represent a functional readout of individual xenobiotic-metabolising capacity and could potentially be used to help predict inter-individual differences in drug metabolism. XENOPRED will investigate whether these findings can be translated into a multi-omics predictive platform designed to estimate individual drug metabolism profiles by integrating (1) PREDICT-CARE derived metabolic signatures, (2) polygenic risk scores reflecting human enzymatic capacity, and (3) microbiome-derived scores capturing microbial enzymatic potential. It will focus on two clinically relevant phenolic drugs, ibuprofen and paracetamol, to assess the predictive accuracy, feasibility, and translational potential of this approach. Generalisability will be explored across other phenolic drugs, including irinotecan (cancer), levothyroxine (thyroid), and chlorpromazine (psychosis), for which evidence on colonic metabolism and inter-individual variability remains limited. The project aims to develop and validate an integration-ready computational module for pharmaceutical R&D workflows and future clinical decision-support tools. By testing a safe, scalable, and cost-effective approach to stratifying individuals according to their metabolic capacity, XENOPRED aims to support safer prescribing, reduce development costs, and accelerate the uptake of personalised health solutions.

title: Reprogramming inflammation via the  DNA damage response-Metabolic axis control
objective: Chronic inflammation underlies autoimmune diseases, cancer, and aging. Yet current therapies fail to address underlying metabolic dysregulation of one-carbon metabolism (1C) or unresolved DNA damage triggering oxidative DNA damage response (OxDDR) that fuel persistent immune activation cycles. Here, we want to decode and target the one-carbon metabolism–oxidative DNA damage response (1C–OxDDR) axis, a critical but underexplored driver of persistent immune activation. We hypothesize that chronic DNA damage and rewired 1C metabolism enforce stable, disease-promoting immune phenotypes. To test this, we will map 1C–OxDDR circuits in patient tissues and aging models using multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and metabolic flux profiling to define signatures of disease initiation, progression, and therapy resistance. We will identify novel disease drivers and develop precision small molecules, leveraging our track record in developing first-in-class inhibitors to MTHFD1&2, OGG1 and MTH1 using an AI-integrated drug design. Furthermore, we will pioneer catalytic medicine through OGG1 amplizymes, introducing a new therapeutic paradigm that introduces novel enzymatic functions to proteins rather than inhibiting them. These strategies will be validated in advanced preclinical systems, including organoids and humanized models to reprogram immune dysfunction without broad immunosuppression. This high-risk/high-gain program builds on our success in synthetic lethality and PARP inhibitors, aiming to deliver a new precision medicine platform for inflammation-driven diseases. By integrating mechanistic insight with innovative medicinal chemistry, RECODE seeks to break the vicious cycle of chronic inflammation, opening therapeutic opportunities across auto-immunity, cancer, and aging, with impact comparable to our previously discovered paradigm-shifting cancer therapies.

title: Teaming to Drive the Future of Genomic Medicine
objective: Genomic medicine is transforming healthcare through precise, personalized solutions that enhance patient outcomes. However, Portugal faces significant challenges, including limited genomic sequencing, fragmented clinical applications, and a shortage of specialized talent. i3S-HEALTH aims to address these issues by modernizing the Institute for Research and Innovation in Health (i3S) into a global Centre of Excellence in Genomic Medicine under the guidance of the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) as an advanced partner. i3S-HEALTH will establish a state-of-the-art Genomic Medicine Hub that uniquely integrates next-generation sequencing, computational biology, AI-driven bioinformatics, and high-throughput functional genomics for new variants discovery to improve patient care. This initiative will be Portugal's first multidisciplinary platform connecting advanced genomic research with clinical diagnostics. Key expected outcomes will include expanded diagnostic capacity and accuracy, trained specialists, developing novel predictive algorithms for complex genetic conditions, and identifying actionable multi-omics biomarkers. i3S-HEALTH will enrich the genomic medicine landscape in Portugal and Europe by strategically engaging the scientific community to accelerate genomic discoveries and foster high-impact collaborations with healthcare providers, improving clinical decision-making through better diagnostics and personalized patient care. It will also collaborate with industry to co-develop innovative diagnostics and therapeutics in public-private partnerships. Increased revenues from advanced diagnostic services, strategic industry partnerships, new projects, IP development, and the launch of genomics spin-offs will ensure sustainability beyond the project. i3S-HEALTH will directly strengthen national R&I performance in genomic medicine, positioning i3S as a leading European center for innovation and excellence in genomic healthcare research.

title: Understanding how the host immunity, the microbiome and environmental stressors shape the ecology and evolution of horizontal transmissible cancers in marine bivalves.
objective: Horizontal transmissible cancers can be passed from one individual to another through malignant cancer cell lines. Such cancers induce leukemia-like cancer in marine bivalves, termed bivalve transmissible neoplasia (BTN). While most BTN lineages are confined to a single host species, some are able to infect multiple species, as demonstrated by my previous work. Host immunity is a known central gatekeeper against BTN, but additional factors have a role in cancer progression, including the host microbiome and the surrounding environment. The interplay of these three factors in driving BTN remains unexplored in the marine ecosystem.I hypothesize that host immunity, the bivalve microbiome, and environmental stressors such as salinity and temperature together define the ecological niche that determines whether BTN cells can persist within common cockles and cross into closely related bivalve species. Through Bivalve2bivalve, I will employ integrative multi-omics approaches to disentangle how these three drivers shape the persistence and transmission potential of BTN. Specifically, this project will:1) Test whether host immune responses restrict or permit BTN persistence, and identify the cellular and molecular pathways underlying this interaction.2) Determine if variation in the cockle-associated microbiome influences susceptibility or resistance to BTN, and identify microbial taxa and functions linked to outcomes.3) Evaluate how environmental stressors such as salinity and temperature interact with immunity and microbiome constituents to modulate BTN persistence and cross-species transmission. Bivalve2bivalve will establish a conceptual framework for understanding transmissible cancers and deepen our knowledge of how hosts, their microbiomes, and the environment shape disease ecology.
